COMPLETE EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; nothing has been executed; no empirical results are reported)

RESEARCH QUESTION
"Does fusing operations within the Adam optimizer (as done in TorchOpt) result in a less complex and more interpretable gradient graph compared to the output from TorchViz?"

Operationalized hypothesis (H1): For an identical optimizer input/output function (same parameters, gradients, optimizer state, and hyperparameters), the autograd graph TorchViz renders from a differentiable Adam update built on TorchOpt's fused kernels has fewer nodes, fewer edges, fewer distinct operator types, and lower depth than the graph TorchViz renders from an equivalent unfused, plain-PyTorch Adam update, while producing numerically equivalent updates — i.e., the graph-size reduction is attributable to fusing alone and improves structural interpretability. H0: no material difference, or the difference disappears once numerical equivalence and graph-instrumentation validity are controlled.

Scope note (explicit interpretation): The only non-trivial reading of "gradient graph" is the autograd graph TorchViz renders when differentiating THROUGH the optimizer update step (TorchOpt's differentiable-optimization/hypergradient use case). Fusing Adam cannot change a model's own loss→params backward graph (it is identical in both arms by construction), so comparing only `make_dot(loss, model.parameters())` would trivially answer "no difference." The design therefore isolates the optimizer-update computation as a pure differentiable function and compares its TorchViz-rendered graph under an unfused vs fused implementation. This scope is documented and tested by a sanity control (C3).

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. RATIONALE (why this design answers the question)
• Cause isolation: The only factor differing between arms is the internal implementation of the Adam update (fused vs unfused). Model, data, seeds, hyperparameters, leaves, and the renderer are all held fixed, so any measured graph difference is attributable to fusing.
• Falsifiability: All primary outcomes are programmatically parsed from the rendered DOT (node/edge/op-type/depth counts) — objective, version-pinned, and reproducible — with an in-advance conclusion rule (Section 5).
• Equivalence control breaks the alternative explanation that "fusing changes the math": if updates are not numerically equivalent, the comparison is confounded and the design flags this instead of silently comparing different optimizers.
• Interpretability is operationalized two ways: structural proxies (primary, falsifiable) computed from the same DOT, and a supplementary rubric-based human-rater pass (qualitative, reported but not load-bearing for the conclusion).

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2. SETUP AND ARMS

2.1 Canonical model & task (deliberately small so graphs are inspectable and node counts tractable)
• Model: 2-hidden-layer MLP with input 8 → hidden [32,16] → output 1, tanh activations (ReLU also acceptable; tanh chosen for smooth, standard non-linearity). Parameters: one Linear(8,32), one Linear(32,16), one Linear(16,1) — small enough that DOT parsing and rendering complete in seconds.
• Task: synthetic regression. X ~ N(0, I_8) (deterministic RNG), y = target_fn(X) + small noise, target_fn fixed (e.g., a fixed random Linear map or a known nonlinear function). Batch size 32.
• Loss: mean squared error.

2.2 Determinism
• torch.manual_seed(seed), numpy seed, and python seed set once per replicate at the top of main(). Model init occurs after seeding. Data generation after seeding. Optimizer state init after seeding. All CPU-only (no GPU; environment is CPU-only anyway), no nondeterministic algorithms (torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True) if supported), thread count fixed.
• Seeds: {0, 1, 2} (3 replicates). Everything inside a replicate is identical across the two arms. Arms share the SAME param tensors, same detached grads, and same state — only the update function differs.

2.3 The two arms (head-to-head on identical I/O)
Common I/O contract for the differentiable update f:
  input: params (leaf tensors), grads (detached leaf tensors), state {m, v} (leaf tensors),
  hyperparameters: lr = 1e-3, betas = (0.9, 0.999), eps = 1e-8, weight_decay = 0.0;
  output: new_params (non-leaf tensor depending on leaves) and new_state.
• Arm A — REFERENCE ("TorchViz output", unfused): plain-PyTorch differentiable Adam in explicit per-parameter form:
    m = beta1*m + (1-beta1)*g ; v = beta2*v + (1-beta2)*g*g ; mhat = m/(1-beta1^t) ; vhat = v/(1-beta2^t) ; p_new = p - lr*mhat/(sqrt(vhat)+eps)
  written as normal torch ops (add, mul, pow, sqrt, div, sub). This is exactly the many-elementwise-node graph TorchViz draws for an unfused Adam. t (step counter) is a fixed integer leaf in both arms.
• Arm B — TREATMENT (TorchOpt fused Adam): the TorchOpt functional Adam update (e.g., `torchopt.optim.adam.adam(...)` returning an update_fn, or TorchOpt's fused/foreach variant — exact API pinned at implementation time, see Section 6.2). The same I/O contract: `update_fn(grads, state, params) -> (updates, state)` or equivalent. If a fused variant is not differentiable through in the installed build, fall back to the documented branch in Section 6.2 (detached-leaf isolation remains valid; this is flagged as a scope limitation, not a silent change).
• TorchViz is the RENDERER IN BOTH ARMS. Rendering setting fixed: `torchviz.make_dot(scalar, params=list(params)+list(grads)+list(state_leaves), show_attrs=False, show_saved=False)`. The scalar must depend on all leaves so the graph is complete: `scalar = new_params.pow(2).sum()`.

2.4 Captured steps
• Step 1 (primary): first optimizer update. Protocol per replicate and per arm:
    a) seed; init model; draw batch; compute loss = mse(model(x), y).
    b) grads = torch.autograd.grad(loss, model.parameters(), create_graph=True) — create_graph=True retained in case the hypergradient path is wanted; for the primary isolation the grads are additionally detached before feeding the update so they are graph leaves (identical across arms).
    c) state init {m=0, v=0}; new_params = update(params, grads, state).
    d) scalar = new_params.pow(2).sum(); dot = make_dot(scalar, ...); capture DOT string and render PNG.
    e) Also capture the model-backward-only graph: make_dot(loss, params) (control C3).
• Optional step 2 (secondary, same protocol repeated once through the optimizer): verifies that the graph differences persist/compound when the update is applied to params that themselves carry history. Kept optional to bound scope; if run, it is run in both arms under the same protocol.

2.5 Run matrix (bounded)
• model config: 1 (canonical); optional second config (e.g., widths [64,32,8]) to check robustness.
• seeds: {0,1,2} → 3 paired replicates.
• steps: 1 (primary), 2 (optional).
• Total primary cells: 1 config × 3 seeds × 2 arms = 6 DOT captures (+3 backward-only sanity DOTs).

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3. METRIC DEFINITIONS

Parsing: the captured DOT string is parsed with pydot, converted to a directed networkx.DiGraph. Node type labels are normalized by stripping trailing integers (e.g., `AddBackward0`→`AddBackward`) and the class-name prefix (e.g., `FusedAdamBackward` → keep as is). Op nodes = nodes whose normalized label endswith `Backward` (or a registered custom Function Backward name); leaf nodes = tensors listed in the `params=` argument plus accumulated-grad leaves.

3.1 Complexity (primary quantitative outcome — all from one DOT object, both arms, identical parsing)
• N  = number of op nodes, |V_op|.
• E  = number of directed edges in the full graph, |E|.
• T  = op-type diversity = number of distinct normalized op-type labels, |{label_v}|.
• H  = Shannon entropy over the op-type histogram: H = −Σ_t p_t·log2 p_t, p_t = count(t)/N.
• D  = depth = number of edges on the longest directed path from any source leaf to the single sink (scalar output) — computed as networkx DAG longest path length.
• W  = width = max over topological levels k of the number of nodes at level k, where level = distance from the sink in the reverse topological order.
• degree stats: mean and max in-degree and out-degree over op nodes.
Each value is computed with one fixed parser call used for both arms (never by eyeballing images).

3.2 Interpretability
Structural proxies (primary, computed from the same DOT as above):
• Semantic-node fraction S = |V_semantic| / |V_op|, with V_semantic defined by a fixed, pre-declared whitelist: labels containing `Fused`, `foreach`, `Adam`, `Optimizer`, or any custom registered Function name produced by TorchOpt (whitelist finalized during the instrument-validation step and written into the script as a constant). High-level/semantic nodes are those mapping to a meaningful named kernel/group operation; everything else is treated as low-level elementwise (Add/Mul/Sqrt/Div/Pow/Sub Backward). Lower S = more visually redundant low-level nodes = less interpretable layout.
• Per-type node share: table of count and share per normalized op type (shows that e.g., in Arm A the same elementwise ops repeat across the graph).
• Optional proxy: number of graph "knots" a reader must visit on the loss→update→params path (approximated by the size of the dominator node set on the main path; reported if computed).
Supplementary human-rater pass (qualitative, reported but NOT part of the conclusion rule):
• Render both arms' PNGs at fixed DPI (e.g., 150) for the canonical cell. ≥2 raters, blind to arm, score 1–5 (Likert) on: (i) ease of tracing loss→update→params; (ii) share of visually redundant/low-level clusters; (iii) naming clarity of nodes; (iv) overall readability. Report mean scores per item per arm and inter-rater agreement (e.g., Krippendorff's alpha) — descriptive only.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4. CONTROLS AND EQUIVALENCE CHECKS

• C1 numerical equivalence (primary confound control): run both update paths on identical detached params/grads/state (create_graph=False copies), compare new_params. Report max|Δ| = max_i|p_A,i − p_B,i| and normalized max|Δ| / max|p|. PASS threshold (pre-declared): normalized max|Δ| ≤ 1e-6. Fused kernels can reorder float ops, so if the threshold is slightly violated only from float order (all deltas ~1e-8 relative), record the actual tolerance and note it; a large divergence (e.g., >1e-4 in normalized units) marks the comparison CONFOUNDED and the treatment arm is re-checked for hyperparameter/API misconfiguration before any conclusion about graph size is drawn.
• C2 paired design / determinism: same seeds, same params, same grads, same state, same hyperparameters in both arms within each replicate → differences within a replicate are attributable to the update implementation alone.
• C3 model-backward sanity check (interpretation scope): make_dot(loss, params) (before any update) must yield identical DOT node/edge counts in both arms. This confirms fusing does not touch the model's own backward graph and documents the scope ("gradient graph" difference = optimizer-update path).
• C4 leaf identity: the `params=` argument lists the same leaf tensors in both arms; report N_leaves (params + grads + state) explicitly for transparency.
• C5 rendering constancy: same torchviz version, same make_dot options (show_attrs=False, show_saved=False), same renderer/DPI for PNGs, same parser and normalized-label function — so DOT-to-graph transformation cannot bias arm differences.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5. ANALYSIS PLAN AND IN-ADVANCE CONCLUSION RULE

Per replicate (paired — same seed in both arms), compute effect sizes:
• ratios R_N = N_B/N_A, R_E = E_B/E_A, R_T = T_B/T_A, R_D = D_B/D_A, R_H = H_B/H_A, ΔS = S_B − S_A.
Aggregate across seeds: mean ± SD of each ratio; if step 2 ran, report step 1 and step 2 separately (step 2 as secondary).
Primary outcomes (pre-registered): R_N (node count) and R_T (op-type diversity).

In-advance conclusion rule:
• SUPPORT H1 if ALL of: (a) mean R_N and mean R_T are materially < 1 — pre-declared threshold: mean R_N ≤ 0.7 (≥30% fewer nodes) and mean R_T ≤ 0.8 (≥20% fewer op types) at step 1, with the reduction in the same direction for all 3 seeds (paired monotonicity); (b) C1 passes (normalized max|Δ| ≤ 1e-6); (c) C3 passes (backward-only graphs identical). Also report R_E, R_D, ΔS as supporting evidence.
• WEAK/MIXED SUPPORT if a) holds but the reduction is below threshold or not monotonic: report effect sizes honestly, no categorical claim.
• NO SUPPORT/reject if a) fails, or if C1 fails (comparison confounded — then no graph-size claim can be made about fusing alone).
• Interpretability claim: report S per arm; claim "structurally more interpretable" only if ΔS ≥ +0.2 (mean) AND rater pass is directionally consistent; otherwise report interpretability as descriptive.

Reporting format (no empirical values manufactured — the design specifies what the report table will contain):
Per cell (config × step): a table of [N, E, T, H, D, W, S] for Arm A, Arm B, ratio, across 3 seeds (mean ± SD), plus C1 deltas and C3 counts. A short narrative converts the table into a SUPPORT / WEAK / NO-SUPPORT verdict per the rule above.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
6. FEASIBILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION-TIME PREREQUISITES

6.1 Pinned environment (to be satisfied at implementation; this workspace cannot install/run them)
• Python 3.10–3.12 (torch/torchopt may not support the workspace's 3.14.4; the design is environment-agnostic and only needs a working torch stack).
• torch ~= 2.3 (any 2.x with stable autograd and _foreach_* support); torchviz ~= 0.0.2; torchopt ~= 0.7.x; pydot ~= 2.x; networkx ~= 3.x; graphviz (system binary, for PNG rendering); numpy.
• No network at implementation time is still fine IF wheels are preinstalled or vendored; if not, the validation steps below can be partially automated but need the packages present.

6.2 TorchOpt fused-Adam validation step (must run and pass before any graph capture)
1) Identify the installed TorchOpt fused Adam entry point (e.g., `torchopt.optim.adam.adam(lr=..., eps=...)` returning (init_fn, update_fn), or a fused/foreach variant; also check whether `update_fn` uses `torch._foreach_*` or a custom `autograd.Function`, and confirm its backward class name for the whitelist).
2) Differentiability-through-update probe: `g = torch.autograd.grad(update_fn(grads,state,params)[0].pow(2).sum(), [params[0]], retain_graph=True)` must succeed and produce finite grads. 
   • If PASS → primary protocol (grads as leaves, full hypergradient-capable path). 
   • If FAIL (fused kernel not differentiable through) → FALLBACK BRANCH (still valid, but flagged in results as scope-limited): feed grads as detached leaves only, i.e., the primary protocol already uses detached grads; the graph still shows the update function's backward structure. The conclusion is then scoped to "update-path graph, grads treated as inputs" — a documented limitation, not a broken experiment.
3) Smoke instrumentation check (NOT a result): on a tiny random instance, confirm the parser detects a larger N in Arm A than Arm B and that both DOTs parse without error — this validates the tooling pipeline before any seeded run.
4) Whitelist finalization: capture Arm B's node labels once and register any custom Function names (e.g., `FusedAdamBackward`, foreach-backed names) into V_semantic as a script constant.

6.3 Short validation checklist (all must be green before interpreting the outcome)
[ ] Pinned deps import successfully (torch, torchviz, torchopt, pydot, networkx).
[ ] TorchOpt fused-Adam entry point found; differentiability probe passes (or fallback engaged and recorded).
[ ] Determinism: re-running one replicate twice yields byte-identical DOT strings for the same arm.
[ ] C1 numerical-equivalence probe passes (or tolerance recorded).
[ ] C3 backward-only graph is invariant to arm.
[ ] Parser handles both DOTs; op-type histogram matches a manual spot-check of a handful of node labels.
[ ] Whitelist constant covers Arm B's semantic node names.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
7. RUNNABLE-IN-PRINCIPLE PYTHON SCRIPT SKELETON (deterministic seeds; API specifics pinned in section 6 before running)

```python
import torch, numpy as np, torch.nn as nn
import pydot, networkx as nx
# torchviz import + torchopt import resolved at implementation time per Section 6.2

SEEDS = [0, 1, 2]
LR, B1, B2, EPS = 1e-3, 0.9, 0.999, 1e-8
RENDER_OPTS = dict(show_attrs=False, show_saved=False)

def set_seed(seed):
    torch.manual_seed(seed); np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)  # if supported by the installed torch

def build_data(seed):
    set_seed(seed)
    X = torch.randn(32, 8); w = torch.randn(8, 1)
    y = X @ w + 0.01 * torch.randn(32, 1)
    return X, y

def build_model(seed):
    set_seed(seed)
    return nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(8,32), nn.Tanh(), nn.Linear(32,16),
                         nn.Tanh(), nn.Linear(16,1))

def unfused_adam_update(params, grads, state, t):
    m, v = state; g = grads                      # elementwise, many nodes (Arm A)
    m = B1*m + (1-B1)*g
    v = B2*v + (1-B2)*g*g
    mhat = m / (1 - B1**t); vhat = v / (1 - B2**t)
    return [(p - LR*mhat/(vhat.sqrt()+EPS)) for p in params], (m, v)

def arm_B_update(params, grads, state, t):
    # TorchOpt fused/functional Adam (API pinned in Section 6.2)
    raise NotImplementedError("pinned at implementation time")  # e.g. init_fn, update_fn = torchopt.optim.adam(...)

def dot_to_metrics(dot_str):
    g = nx.DiGraph(pydot.graph_from_dot_data(dot_str)[0].to_undirected())
    # direction: pydot edges -> DiGraph; normalize labels; classify op vs leaf
    # compute N, E, T, H (entropy over op-type hist), D (dag_longest_path_length),
    # W (max level size), S (semantic share via whitelist)  -> dict
    raise NotImplementedError("canonical implementation; see Section 3 formulas")

def capture(update_fn, params, grads, state, t, name):
    from torchviz import make_dot
    new_params, _ = update_fn(params, grads, state, t)
    scalar = sum(p.pow(2).sum() for p in new_params)          # depends on all leaves
    dot_args = params + grads + list(state)
    dot = make_dot(scalar, params=dot_args, **RENDER_OPTS)
    dot.render(f"{name}_graph", format="png")                  # PNG for rater pass
    return dot.to_string(), scalar

def run_replicate(seed):
    set_seed(seed); X, y = build_data(seed)   # deterministic
    model = build_model(seed); params = list(model.parameters())
    loss = ((model(X) - y) ** 2).mean()
    grads = torch.autograd.grad(loss, params, create_graph=True)    # then detached as leaves below
    grads = [g.detach().clone().requires_grad_() for g in grads]
    m0 = [torch.zeros_like(p) for p in params]; v0 = [torch.zeros_like(p) for p in params]
    dotA, _ = capture(unfused_adam_update, params, grads, (m0, v0), 1, f"armA_s{seed}")
    dotB, _ = capture(arm_B_update,        params, grads, (m0, v0), 1, f"armB_s{seed}")
    # C1 numerical equivalence on detached copies
    pA, _ = unfused_adam_update(params, [g.detach() for g in grads], (m0, v0), 1)
    pB, _ = arm_B_update(        params, [g.detach() for g in grads], (m0, v0), 1)
    delta = max((a-b).abs().max().item() for a,b in zip(pA,pB)) / max(p.abs().max().item() for p in params)
    # C3 backward-only invariance
    dotA_back = make_dot(loss, params=params, **RENDER_OPTS); dotB_back = make_dot(loss, params=params, **RENDER_OPTS)
    return dict(msA=dot_to_metrics(dotA), msB=dot_to_metrics(dotB), c1=delta, c3=(dotA_back.to_string()==dotB_back.to_string()))

def main():
    results = {s: run_replicate(s) for s in SEEDS}
    # Section 5 reporting: per-cell ArmA/ArmB tables, ratios R_N,R_E,R_T,R_D,R_H,dS,
    # mean+/-SD over seeds; verdict per the in-advance rule. (No values printed here.)
```

Notes on the skeleton: every captured artifact (DOT + PNG) is written to disk with the seed/arm name for auditability; the `arm_B_update` call is intentionally a pinned-`NotImplementedError` placeholder because the exact TorchOpt fused API can only be confirmed on a machine with the package installed (validation step 6.2). Nothing above has been executed in this workspace; the skeleton is provided as an in-principle, runnable-after-pinning specification.
